ratings_why.fun: The curve has a real shape: small Debt tricks early, Thought and Memory and Sorrow and Joy pop at Tier 4, and Corbie's Ledger accelerates late, with four builds that pull against each other.
ratings_why.distinct: Debt as a number you want high in the fight and low at the bill is unlike any of today's tribes, though the payoffs are mostly familiar +X/+X buffers.

verdict_why: The rules now read cleanly and every tier does its job; what's left is hot numbers for the owner to balance, not fixes.

points.text: The Racket snowballs: a won fight skims Tower Raven's and Slate-Drinker Rook's Debt away, so borrowing becomes free gold plus Seven and Sorrow and Joy buffs, while a lost fight leaves a bill. Losing is the counterplay, which is fine, but it's the line to sim first.

Penny Jackdaw's early tempo is weak in a game where rounds 1-3 deal no hero damage, and it makes turn 2 broke. Something like 'Borrow 3 once; your next Refresh is free' would let it win early fights without the dead turn.

Slate-Drinker Rook borrows at End of Turn, after you've shopped, so off the Racket it costs 1 gold a turn for +1/+1. Borrowing at Start of Combat instead, like Tower Raven, would keep the job and stop it feeling like a tax.
Mr Magpie's row switch is the tribe's best decision: when to call the bill in. A small visible 'bill next turn' preview on the card would make that call readable at a glance.
Belfry Mob gives Skim to non-Syndicate units, but Seven and Silas Glint only count Syndicate Skims. That's a fair splash rule; a one-line reminder on Seven would stop players feeling cheated.

standouts.why: Thought and Memory multiplies repayments, not stats, so it lifts whichever build you chose; a clean Tier 4 multiplier.
Mr Magpie turns board position into a timing switch for the bill; free, visible and very distinctive.
Seven is a satisfying capstone: every kill pays the family and grows the board, and Debt caps it so you must keep borrowing.

weakest.why: Penny Jackdaw buys tempo when tempo matters least and leaves a broke turn after.
Slate-Drinker Rook is still a slow gold leak outside the Racket.
Oast Bookkeeper spends gold to repay early, which most turns you'd rather spend on units; its buff only matters late.

flags.note: Sorrow and Joy has no limit, so with Belfry Mob Skims and Thought and Memory it can give about 50 stats a fight, several times a Tier 4 target.
Tower Raven plus Skimmers plus Silas Glint can be 5+ free gold a won fight; win-more economy that could snowball.
Arne with Thought and Memory on a Mr Magpie lump of 12 is roughly +12/+12 to the tribe in one turn; the designed high roll, worth the owner's eye.
